content.text:
I couldn't read any source files. The snippets show only the call graph, so this diagnosis is inferred from the structure and not confirmed against the code.

Login and refresh both work, so tokens are being issued and the refresh strategy (`JwtRefreshStrategy`) accepts the refresh token. Only the access-token check (`JwtStrategy`) rejects the token, so the defect is most likely in that strategy or in how `getTokensData` signs the access token.

candidates.explanation: The access-token strategy is configured here with the extractor and secretOrKey. If it reads the wrong secret (for example auth.refreshSecret instead of auth.secret), or the wrong extraction or expiry option, every access token that AuthService signed fails verification. Passport then returns 401, while login and refresh still work because they use the refresh strategy and secret.

validate() decides whether the decoded payload is accepted. If it checks the wrong payload field (for example payload.userId instead of payload.id) or returns a falsy value, it throws UnauthorizedException for every fresh token.

This method signs the access token. If it signs with the wrong secret (such as the refresh or forgot secret), or puts the wrong claims in the payload (the id key or the session id), JwtStrategy cannot verify or accept it. Refresh tokens would still be fine.

fix.description: Make the JwtStrategy constructor use the same secret as getTokensData uses to sign access tokens (configService.getOrThrow('auth.secret')), not the refresh secret. Make validate() check the same payload field that getTokensData puts in the token (payload.id) and return the payload. Make sure getTokensData signs the access token with auth.secret and auth.expires.
